[M157] [omnibox][webui] Suppress AIM button focus for keywords and actions

Original change's description:
> [omnibox][webui] Suppress AIM button focus for keywords and actions
>
> Previously, `SearchboxSelectionMixin.getAvailableSelections()`
> unconditionally inserted `SelectionLineState.kFocusedButtonAim` at index
> 1 when the AIM button was visible.
>
> If the default match had an associated keyword chip or action chips
> (e.g. switch to this tab), or if the second match had an instant keyword
> (e.g. user typed '@'), pressing Tab would focus the AIM button first
> instead of entering keyword mode or focusing the action, disrupting user
> muscle memory.
>
> This CL aligns WebUI selection logic with the traditional Views Omnibox
> (`OmniboxPopupSelection::GetAllAvailableSelectionsSorted()`) by
> suppressing the AIM button selection when:
> - The default match has an associated keyword chip.
> - The default match has action chips.
> - The second match has an instant keyword (`KeywordType.kInstant`).
>

[M157] [Omnibox] Defer WebUI suggestion popup creation

Original change's description:
> [Omnibox] Defer WebUI suggestion popup creation
>
> Design doc:
> https://docs.google.com/document/d/1P7h7q6zqhxgPtKhVJBUAU9eb1pawDwK66iQu8CTeRSs/edit?resourcekey=0-nPCcl7S22YgfphQ-H6WV5Q&tab=t.0
>
> When a browser window is built, OmniboxPopupPresenter creates the WebUI
> suggestion popup's content in its constructor: a WebContents and its
> navigation to the popup page. Like the AI Mode popup, this work
> competes with the new window's first frame on the browser UI thread
> and in the shared top-chrome renderer.
>
> This CL adds a disabled-by-default feature,
> OmniboxWebUIPopupDeferCreation, separate from
> OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation so that the two popups can be evaluated
> independently. It reuses the deferral support that the parent CL adds
> to OmniboxPopupPresenterBase: the presenter overrides
> CreateWebUIContent(), and the content is created by whichever of these
> comes first:
>
> - A task posted after the browser window's first successful
>   presentation. LocationBarView and WebUILocationBar now also pass
>   OnBrowserWindowPresented() to the suggestion popup's presenter.
> - OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::Show(), when the user types before the
>   task runs.
>
> Nothing else reads the suggestion popup content before it is shown:
> OmniboxPopupViewWebUI reads it right after Show(), and its selection
> methods run only while the popup is open. As with the AI Mode popup, no
> fallback timer is needed.
>
> The cost is that typing before the content exists makes the first popup
> open wait for the page to load, which is why this popup has its own
> feature.
>
> With the feature disabled, creation is unchanged.
>
> The AI Mode popup test for the classic popup's context menu now creates
> the classic content first, because that content may be deferred too.
>
>   out/Default/browser_tests --gtest_filter='OmniboxWebUIPopup*'
>   and without --enable-features=OmniboxWebUIPopupDeferCreation
>

[M157] Clear window rootViewController after disconnecting scene state

Original change's description:
> Clear window rootViewController after disconnecting scene state
>
> In SceneDelegate sceneDidDisconnect, setting the window's
> rootViewController to nil before setting the scene state activation
> level to SceneActivationLevelDisconnected causes UIKit to immediately
> tear down the active root view controller while child controllers and
> focus environments are still active. This can trigger UIKit focus system
> exceptions during the view controller removal transition.
>
> Transitioning sceneState.activationLevel to
> SceneActivationLevelDisconnected first triggers UI teardown gracefully.
> Clearing rootViewController after setting the activation level allows
> the root view controller to be cleared safely.
>
> This fix was generated by the Crash Autofix pipeline for crash report
> crash/24187a4d08400000. Please see go/crash-autofix for more details.

[M157] [iOS][AppBar] Skip symbol content transition when the App Bar is hidden

Original change's description:
> [iOS][AppBar] Skip symbol content transition when the App Bar is hidden
>
> On iOS 26, calling `-[UIImageView
> setSymbolImage:withContentTransition:]` backs the image view with a
> RenderBox layer whose rendering is performed synchronously on the main
> thread during the next `CATransactionCommit`. The App Bar tab grid
> button performs such a transition on every tab grid enter/exit,
> including on iPad where the App Bar is hidden (`AppBarPosition::kNone`),
> where the animation cannot be seen.
>
> Tracing the tab grid round trip on a Release simulator build showed
> RenderBox work (`RB::SharedSurfaceGroup::render_updates`, Metal pipeline
> build, GPU waits) only with ChromeNextIa, inflating the first tab grid
> open to ~360ms and `CATransactionCommit` to ~65ms; using a plain image
> swap removed all RenderBox activity and brought both back to baseline.
>
> This CL adds `kAppBarStaticSymbolWhenHidden`. When enabled, the tab grid
> symbol is set with `-setImage:` while the App Bar is not visible (no
> position in the scene layout or not attached to a window); the animated
> content transition is kept whenever the App Bar can be seen. With the
> flag disabled the behavior is unchanged.
>

[M157] Disable FEDisplacementMap acting as a backdrop-filter

Original change's description:
> Disable FEDisplacementMap acting as a backdrop-filter
>
> The background contents filtered by a CSS backdrop filter may contain
> sensitive information, including but not limited to forms containing
> user data or cross-origin image content. When the background is used as
> the displacement map for an SVG FEDisplacementMap filter it becomes
> possible to use timing attacks to determine the background, so the spec
> says the filter must operate as a pass through when the map input is
> cross-origin or otherwise should not be revealed.
>
> Unfortunately we cannot just taint all backdrop filters because doing so
> disables them for HTML-in-Canvas. Instead, add tracking of "contains
> backdrop" to the filter effect chain and use it in FEDisplacementMap to
> enforce pass-through.
>

[m157][ios] Clear underlying scroll view delegate in scroll view proxy dealloc

When CRWWebViewScrollViewProxy is deallocated during WebState teardown
(where clearContentViewAndAddPlaceholder:NO skips calling
-setScrollView:nil), -[CRWWebViewScrollViewProxy dealloc] stops KVO
observations on underlyingScrollView but does not clear its delegate.

When CRWWebViewScrollViewDelegateProxy is subsequently deallocated,
WKScrollView's weak _externalDelegate pointer is zeroed without calling
-[WKScrollView setDelegate:nil]. This leaves
WKScrollViewDelegateForwarder installed as UIScrollView.delegate with
the cached delegateScrollViewDidChangeAdjustedContentInset bitflag
still set. On iOS 18, WKWebView (_internalDelegate) does not implement
-scrollViewDidChangeAdjustedContentInset:, causing an unrecognized
selector exception if adjustedContentInset changes before WKWebView
finishes deallocating.

Explicitly call [self.underlyingScrollView setDelegate:nil] in
-[CRWWebViewScrollViewProxy dealloc] to match -setScrollView:.

[M157] [omnibox] Keep focus on the page after submitting from the AIM popup

Original change's description:
> [omnibox] Keep focus on the page after submitting from the AIM popup
>
> With the Full WebUI omnibox, submitting a query from the AIM popup
> navigated the tab but left keyboard focus in the omnibox, with the Full
> WebUI popup reopened on top of the results page.
>
> Submitting a query from the popup closes it from
> `ContextualSearchboxHandler::OpenUrl()`, which sets the popup state to
> `kNone`, reverts the location bar and focuses the tab's WebContents.
> Hiding the AIM popup then asks the page for its draft via the async
> `ClearPopup()` IPC. When the reply arrives,
> `OmniboxAimPopupWebUIContent::ApplyInputAndCleanup()` hands focus back
> to the omnibox whenever the browser window is active, a path added by
> crrev.com/c/8427468 so that closing the AIM popup (e.g. by clicking
> the page) returns to the omnibox with the draft. Because the browser
> window is active right after a submission too, the omnibox reclaimed
> focus from the results page and reopened the Full WebUI popup.
>
> Submitting with a modifier (e.g. Ctrl+Enter or Ctrl+click on a match,
> which open the results in another tab or window) had the same problem
> through a second path: the composebox also closes itself right after
> such a submit, which sends `RequestClose()` and reaches
> `OmniboxAimPopupWebUIContent::CloseUI()`. That explicit close restores
> the draft and hands focus back to the omnibox.
>
> Fix both paths:
> * The AIM page reports whether a query was submitted since the popup
>   was last shown, as a new `query_submitted` field in the
>   `ClearPopup()` reply. `ApplyInputAndCleanup()` skips handing focus
>   back to the omnibox in that case.
> * `closeComposebox()` marks the close it fires right after a submit
>   with `afterSubmit` in the `close-composebox` event. The AIM page
>   skips `RequestClose()` for such closes, since the browser closes the
>   popup itself for every submit it accepts. Other closes, including an
>   Escape after a submit the browser dropped, still go through.
>
> Explicit WebUI closes (Escape, the cancel button) and click-outside
> closes still restore the draft and focus as before, so the
> flicker-free AIM to Full WebUI handoff is unchanged.
>
> NO_IFTTT=No logic added to composebox.ts, it only forwards a parameter.
>

Original change's description:
> [omnibox] Log WebUI Ctrl+Enter .com navigations as URL navigations
>

> selection on the highlighted line [1]. OmniboxEditModel::OpenSelection()

> ".com" URL_WHAT_YOU_TYPED match, but pass that selection along with it.
> Because the selection's line is in range, OpenMatch() logs the popup's
> matches with the highlighted line selected [2], not the match that was
> opened. OmniboxEventProto records the highlighted match, often
> SEARCH_WHAT_YOU_TYPED, and log observers such as
> AutocompleteActionPredictor see that match instead of the URL.
>
> The Views omnibox opens the generated match with a kNoMatch selection
> [3], so OpenMatch() logs it as the only match. Do the same in both
> places. When no ".com" URL can be generated, Ctrl+Enter still opens the
> highlighted match and logs the popup's matches.
>
> Only the Full WebUI omnibox sends kCtrlEnter on a popup line [4]. The
> SearchboxHandler path only runs with
> kWebUISearchboxWithoutModelController, which is disabled and has no unit
> tests for this flow.

[M157] Reland "[Omnibox] Defer AI Mode popup creation"

Original change's description:
> Reland "[Omnibox] Defer AI Mode popup creation"
>
> This is a reland of commit 7a7e498dbdb75a1c7329d8e7bf4395e3c5832fb2
>
> The original change was reverted because
> OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreationPendingBrowserTest.ClassicPopupContextMenuCreatesAimContent
> crashed on mac26-arm64-rel-tests. The test opened the classic popup's
> context menu while that popup was hidden, so the menu had no parent
> widget, and the Mac menu code dereferences it. Real right-clicks only
> reach a shown popup. The test now shows the classic popup first and
> cancels the menu at the end. The production code is unchanged.
>
> Original change's description:
> > [Omnibox] Defer AI Mode popup creation
> >
> > Design doc:
> > https://docs.google.com/document/d/1P7h7q6zqhxgPtKhVJBUAU9eb1pawDwK66iQu8CTeRSs/edit?resourcekey=0-nPCcl7S22YgfphQ-H6WV5Q&tab=t.0
> >
> > When a browser window is built, OmniboxPopupAimPresenter creates the AI
> > Mode popup's WebUI content in its constructor: a WebContents and its
> > navigation to the AI Mode popup page. The navigation's IPCs and the
> > page load then compete with the new window's first frame on the browser
> > UI thread and in the shared top-chrome renderer. The AI Mode popup is
> > opened far less often than the regular results popup, so it does not
> > need to be ready that early.
> >
> > This CL adds a disabled-by-default feature,
> > OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation. With it, the presenter does not create
> > the content in its constructor. It overrides the new
> > OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::CreateWebUIContent(), and
> > OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::EnsureWebUIContentCreated() calls it on
> > whichever of these comes first:
> >
> > - A task posted after the browser window presents its first frame.
> > - OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::Show().
> > - The regular popup's context menu, which acts on the AI Mode
> >   WebContents.
> >
> > The presenter asks for that frame itself: its constructor makes a
> > one-off RequestSuccessfulPresentationTimeForNextFrame() call on the
> > compositor of the location bar's widget. Both LocationBarView and
> > WebUILocationBar build the presenter while the window is built, before
> > its first paint, so the next frame is the window's first frame. The
> > presenter posts the creation task at most once.
> >
> > The presentation task is what keeps the work out of the window's first
> > frame. A fixed delay from window creation could not do that: on Linux
> > and macOS the window is activated inside its own show call, before the
> > first paint, and the time to first paint varies by device. There is
> > also no fallback timer. A requested callback is kept until a frame
> > presents successfully. A window that is never presented never shows
> > the popup either, and the on-show path covers any open. A presenter
> > that is created after the first paint, because the profile became
> > eligible for AI Mode later, gets the next presented frame or its first
> > show.
> >
> > With the feature disabled, creation is unchanged.
